action: Current and former York students, applicants and staff: watch for a notice from the university, be alert to messages using your details, and monitor accounts if you submitted sensitive information. Other institutions: review how long form data is kept.
date_note: BleepingComputer reported York's confirmation on 9 November; the university says the unauthorised access was discovered on 25 October.
exec: Nearly two decades of retained form data was exposed, showing the risk of keeping personal data longer than needed.
plain: York University said attackers stole personal information that people had submitted through its online forms, going back as far as 2007. The number of people affected has not been given.
summary: York University confirmed the theft of personal information from some departmental forms on 14 of its websites, covering submissions from 2007 to 2026; it says the access was discovered on 25 October. No count of affected people has been given. York will notify those whose government ID or financial account details were exposed.
title: York University breach exposes form submissions dating to 2007

validation.note: York's statement as quoted by BleepingComputer, with Privacy Guides repeating it; York's own notice was not read.

review.note: BleepingComputer (9 Nov) quotes York confirming theft from departmental forms, discovered 25 Oct, 14 websites, 2007-2026. Date moved from 12 Nov roundup date to 9 Nov, sources and summary fixed, correction filed. No record count given.
